entities.name: Knowledge Graph
entities.description: A structured representation of facts about entities and the relationships between them. It organizes information as a graph where nodes represent entities (people, places, organizations, concepts) and edges represent typed relationships between those entities. Each edge carries a specific relationship type, such as 'founded_by', 'located_in', or 'works_at'. Knowledge graphs allow machines to reason about the world in a structured way, enabling applications like question answering, recommendation systems, search engines, and AI assistants.

entities.description: An ontology defines the types of entities and relationships that can exist in a knowledge graph and the logical constraints on how they relate. entities.name: Large Language Models
entities.description: A type of machine learning model trained on vast quantities of text data to understand and generate human language.
entities.source_sentence: A large language model (LLM) is a type of machine learning model trained on vast quantities of text data to understand and generate human language.

entities.name: LLMs
entities.description: Language models, such as BERT and its variants.
entities.source_sentence: LLMs are first pre-trained on a large unlabeled text corpus using a self-supervised objective. The most common objective is next-token prediction (autoregressive language modeling): given the preceding tokens in a sequence, predict the next token. The model learns to minimize the cross-entropy loss between its predicted probability distribution and the actual next token.

entities.name: LLM
entities.description: Language Models
entities.source_sentence: LLMs are typically fine-tuned on curated datasets of instruction-response pairs to improve their ability to follow user instructions. This process, known as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), teaches the model to respond helpfully to prompts rather than simply continuing text.

entities.name: Human
entities.description: Human annotators
entities.source_sentence: Human annotators rank model responses by quality, and these rankings are used to train a reward model. The LLM is then fine-tuned using proximal policy optimization (PPO) to maximize the learned reward signal.

entities.name: RAG
entities.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enhances large language model outputs by grounding them in relevant external documents retrieved at query time.
entities.source_sentence: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enhances large language model outputs by grounding them in relevant external documents retrieved at query time.

entities.name: RAG
entities.description: RAG (Reinforcement Learning Agent) is a large language model that stores knowledge implicitly during training.
entities.source_sentence: Large language models store knowledge implicitly in their weights during training. This creates several problems: the knowledge has a training cutoff date, it can be hallucinated or misremembered, and updating it requires expensive retraining. RAG addresses these issues by keeping knowledge external and retrievable, making it easy to update and verify.

entities.name: Dense Retriever
entities.description: The retriever encodes both queries and documents into dense vector representations using a bi-encoder model. During retrieval, the query vector is compared against all document vectors using approximate nearest neighbor search.
entities.source_sentence: The retriever encodes both queries and documents into dense vector representations using a bi-encoder model. During retrieval, the query vector is compared against all document vectors using approximate nearest neighbor search.

entities.name: Document Store / Vector Index
entities.description: Retrieved documents are stored in a vector index that supports fast approximate nearest neighbor search. Common choices include FAISS (from Facebook AI Research), Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, and LanceDB. The choice of vector store significantly affects retrieval latency and memory usage.

entities.name: Graph RAG
entities.description: Graph RAG is a knowledge graph builder that extracts entities and relationships from the document corpus using an LLM. It supports multi-hop reasoning and flat vector search, making it useful for both local and global queries.
entities.source_sentence: Graph RAG builds a knowledge graph from the document corpus by extracting entities and relationships using an LLM. At query time, it traverses the graph structure to find relevant connected information, enabling multi-hop reasoning that flat vector search cannot support.

entities.description: RAG pipeline is a natural language processing (NLP) system that decomposes the RAG (Relevance-Augmented Generation) pipeline into interchangeable modules for indexing, retrieval, reranking, and generation.

entities.name: Vector databases
entities.description: Text, images, and other unstructured data can be converted into dense vector representations (embeddings) using neural models. These embeddings capture semantic meaning — similar concepts produce vectors that are close together in the high-dimensional embedding space. Vector databases make it possible to search billions of embeddings in milliseconds, enabling semantic search at scale.
entities.source_sentence: Text, images, and other unstructured data can be converted into dense vector representations (embeddings) using neural models. These embeddings capture semantic meaning — similar concepts produce vectors that are close together in the high-dimensional embedding space. Vector databases make it possible to search billions of embeddings in milliseconds, enabling semantic search at scale.

relationships.description: The rise of large language models and embedding models like OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002, Cohere's Embed, and open-source models like nomic-embed-text has driven rapid growth in the vector database market.

entities.name: Embeddings
entities.description: A dense, fixed-length vector (typically 384 to 4096 dimensions) that represents the semantic content of an input.
entities.source_sentence: An embedding is a dense, fixed-length vector (typically 384 to 4096 dimensions) that represents the semantic content of an input.

entities.name: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
entities.description: Exact nearest neighbor search requires comparing a query vector against every stored vector — linear time complexity that becomes prohibitive at billion-vector scale. Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithms trade a small amount of recall for dramatically faster search.
entities.source_sentence: Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithms trade a small amount of recall for dramatically faster search.

entities.name: Cosine similarity
entities.description: measures the angle between two vectors, capturing directional similarity regardless of magnitude. It is the standard metric for text embedding similarity.
entities.source_sentence: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors, capturing directional similarity regardless of magnitude. It is the standard metric for text embedding similarity.

entities.name: Dot product
entities.description: is equivalent to cosine similarity when vectors are normalized. Euclidean (L2) distance measures straight-line distance between points and is common in image embedding applications.
entities.source_sentence: Dot product (inner product) similarity is equivalent to cosine similarity when vectors are normalized. Euclidean (L2) distance measures straight-line distance between points and is common in image embedding applications.

entities.name: Euclidean distance
entities.description: measures straight-line distance between points and is common in image embedding applications.
entities.source_sentence: Euclidean (L2) distance measures straight-line distance between points and is common in image embedding applications.

relationships.description: FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is an open-source library developed by Meta AI Research for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors. It supports multiple index types including IVF, HNSW, and PQ (Product Quantization). FAISS runs entirely in-process — there is no server component — making it suitable for embedded applications and research prototypes. It does not natively support metadata filtering.

entities.name: FAISS
entities.description: A scalable and efficient vector database that supports high-performance search and retrieval.
entities.source_sentence: Vector database performance depends on several factors: index type (HNSW achieves high recall at low latency; IVF is more memory-efficient at scale), dataset size (billion-vector datasets require GPU acceleration or distributed deployment), and hardware (GPU-accelerated search with cuVS or GPU-FAISS can achieve 100x speedup over CPU for large datasets).
